subject: On‑prem pricing clarifications — pilot credit and exit schedule
messages:
From: Asha Menon <asha.m@medisync-health.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@medisync-health.com
Date: 2026-04-18T21:07:00Z
Subject: Questions on on‑prem pricing, pilot credits, and exit terms

Hi Kimberly / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited about Redwood for our inference needs. Before we move the SOW to legal, procurement has a few clarifying asks on the on‑prem (VPC) commercial construct:

1) Pilot credits: can you confirm the pilot credit logic (you mentioned a $75k credit applied to the first-year platform fee, but only if we convert to production within 120 days). We need the exact trigger and whether credits prorate if we convert later.

2) Exit / refund mechanics: our finance team wants an exit protection mechanism if the deployment fails acceptance within 180 days. What level of refund/credit for platform fee and operator licenses is Redwood willing to offer?

3) Support tiers & SLA uplift: can we get a short note on the initial 90‑day hypercare uplift (response times and whether incident credits are automatic or require an RCA)?

4) Hardware escrow / pass‑throughs: because this will be installed in our co‑lo, procurement is asking if Redwood will sign a limited hardware escrow for the operator package or if that is something we own entirely.

If you can send proposed language we can share with our legal and procurement. Ideally a redline of the SOW + term sheet.

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Asha
Director, Procurement
Medisync Health

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Asha Menon <asha.m@medisync-health.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-19T09:12:00Z
Subject: RE: Questions on on‑prem pricing, pilot credits, and exit terms

Hi Asha — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together an email with the proposed commercial positions and attached SOW + pricing sheet (attached). Key points below so procurement/legal have plain language to start with:

- Pilot credit: $75,000 credit applied to the first 12 months' platform fee. Credit vests only on execution of the production conversion form (attached) and is valid if conversion completes within 120 days of pilot go‑live. If conversion happens between day 121–240 the credit is 50% ($37,500). After 240 days the credit expires. We can add a clause allowing a one‑time 30‑day extension for exceptional circumstances (written request).

- Exit / refund schedule (acceptance failure): If Medisync terminates due to failed acceptance within 180 days we will: (a) refund 50% of any pre‑paid platform fee for the remainder of the first 12 months less professional services hours used; (b) operator license fees are refundable on a prorated basis for any unused months after decommissioning but subject to standard transfer restrictions. We propose a simple schedule in the SOW (table in appendix) — redlines attached.

- Support tiers & hypercare: For the initial 90 days we offer an "Enhanced Hypercare" addendum: 24/7 P1 response within 1 hour, named SRE rotation, weekly health check cadence, and automatic incident credits equal to 2% of the monthly platform fee per missed SLO (credit applies up to 3 incidents per month). Credits are applied as invoice adjustments; we can add automatic application language to avoid manual claims.

- Hardware escrow / operator package: Redwood does not place hardware into escrow (co‑lo assets remain customer owned). For the operator package we will provide signed escrow-friendly source code deposit terms for the operator binaries (limited release upon bankruptcy or long‑term failure). We can provide an escrow statement for your legal team; see redline in attached term doc.

I've attached: Medisync_SOW_draft_v2.pdf (redline), pricing-sheet-privdeploy-2026.xlsx, redlines_private_deploy_terms.docx.

DocuSign: I included a placeholder for the conversion form and SOW signature — https://www.docusign.com/recipient?t=abc123-placeholder

If that looks reasonable I can pull together a short amendment with the exact tables and send to legal. Happy to join a procurement call later this week.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Solutions Lead — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Medisync_SOW_draft_v2.pdf (redline), pricing-sheet-privdeploy-2026.xlsx (pricing workbook), redlines_private_deploy_terms.docx (term suggestions)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-19T11:20:00Z
Subject: INTERNAL: Suggested commercial concessions for Medisync

Team — quick internal note before we send anything to legal. Quoting Kimberly below for context. My suggested concessions and rationale: 

- Keep the $75k pilot credit as written but accept the 121–240 day 50% taper. This gives procurement runway without setting a perpetual precedent.

- Exit refund: agree to the 50% refund on pre‑paid platform fee but limit PS deductions to hours invoiced at time of termination (no retro adjustments). Add a "good faith decommission" clause to prevent claims for environment changes.

- Operator license refunds: allow prorated refund only if the license keys are surrendered and all on‑prem artifacts removed (standard).

- Hypercare credits: automatic application is fine but cap any single month's credit impact to 20% of monthly platform fee to protect cashflow. Also require a joint RCA before credits exceed two months of charges.

- Escrow: offer the escrow deposit language but push back on broad release triggers — limit to insolvency or failure to maintain support for 60 continuous days.

If legal wants firmer language on any of these, I can take point on commercial calls. Recommend we offer a 30‑minute call with procurement + legal next Thursday to finalize.

Ben
VP, Enterprise Sales

From: Asha Menon <asha.m@medisync-health.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@medisync-health.com
Date: 2026-04-20T15:30:00Z
Subject: RE: Questions on on‑prem pricing, pilot credits, and exit terms

Kimberly — thanks for the clear write up and the attachments. Procurement/legal reviewed the positions and we can tentatively accept the pilot credit taper and refund schedule with two small asks before we sign:

1) For the 50% refund on prepaid platform fees, can you add a 14‑day notice and remediation period before the refund trigger? Our legal prefers a short cure period to allow a final remediation attempt.

2) For the hypercare credits, we accept automatic application but ask that the cap be 25% of monthly platform fee (rather than 20%) for the initial 90‑day window only. After 90 days it reverts to 20%.

If you can send a 1‑page amendment that reflects the two small items we can circulate for signatures. Also can you confirm the HubSpot deal id (we need it on the PO) — the HubSpot link you sent is perfect.

If agreeable let's schedule the procurement call Thursday 4/22 — 10am PT.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Asha
Director, Procurement
Medisync Health
